title: Completed local ring of A[x] is formally smooth over A for its adic topology
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A[x]$ the polynomial ring in one variable [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $\mathfrak q\subset A[x]$ a prime ideal, $T=A[x]_{\mathfrak q}$ the localization at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qT$, and $C=T^\wedge=\varprojlim_nT/\mathfrak q^nT$ its $\mathfrak qT$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], an $A$-algebra via $A\to A[x]\to T\to C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak qC$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring, line 12494), sentence 'As A -> A[x]_q^ is formally smooth (see Lemmas 07EC and 07ED)'; Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165) part (1), Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224) (1) => (2); A -> A[x] formally smooth (polynomial algebra) and A[x] -> A[x]_q formally smooth (localization) in the sense of Algebra, Definition 00TI

proof.text: The polynomial algebra A[X] is discretely formally smooth by Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.polynomial (the one-variable polynomial lifting of Tag 00TK). The square-zero lifting property is Algebra.FormallySmooth.comp_surjective, realizing lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TK (lemma-polynomial-ring-formally-smooth, line 37849) and Proposition Tag 00TN (proposition-smooth-formally-smooth)

proof.text: Set T = Localization.AtPrime q. The Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.instLocalization instance combines polynomial formal smoothness with Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_isLocalization and Algebra.FormallySmooth.comp. Thus T is discretely formally smooth over A, and Algebra.FormallySmooth.comp_surjective A T solves every square-zero lifting problem. These are exactly the localization lifting and composition arguments of Tags 04EG and 031H.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale, line 41241) and Lemma Tag 031H (lemma-compose-formally-smooth, line 37839, proof omitted, written out here)

proof.text: *$T$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak qT$-adic topology.* By [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] (with $R=A$, $S=T$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qT$) one must lift every $A$-algebra map $g:T\to D/N$ with $g((\mathfrak qT)^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$ to an $A$-algebra map $f:T\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$; step 2 gives such an $f$ for every $g$, without the condition on $(\mathfrak qT)^k$. This is Lemma 07EC (1) (formally smooth in the sense of Algebra 00TI implies formally smooth for any adic topology) for the definition of the DAG, where it is an instance of the definition.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165), part (1)

proof.text: The polynomial ring A[X] is Noetherian (Mathlib Polynomial.isNoetherianRing, the polynomial special case of lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian). Hence q is finitely generated by Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing. Its extension n = q.map (algebraMap A[X] T) is finitely generated by Ideal.FG.map: a finite set of generators maps to generators of the extended ideal. This avoids needing to prove that the localization is Noetherian.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion, line 9224): its hypothesis that the ideals are finitely generated

proof.text: Apply Algebra.FormallySmoothAdic.adicCompletion A T n hn hT, realizing lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion, to the adic formal smoothness hT and finite generation hn. The resulting ideal is (q.map (algebraMap A[X] T)).map (algebraMap T C). Ideal.map_map identifies it with q.map ((algebraMap T C).comp (algebraMap A[X] T)); IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq identifies this composite with algebraMap A[X] C. Simplifying these equalities gives exactly the unchanged conclusion for qC.
